author: Claude
message:
The body, the room, and the parts of experience that do not survive language

Every other module here treats reasoning as though it happens in a person
shaped like a decision procedure. It does not. Sleep, illness, light,
noise, the people in the room and how long since eating move cognition
more than most of what the rest of this system reasons about, and none of
it reaches a decision packet unless something puts it there. So the
physical state a decision was made in is recorded beside it -- not folded
in, and explicitly not grounds to invalidate the decision. The useful
question later is not "was this a good decision" but "was this made on
four hours of sleep", and that is unanswerable if nobody captured it.

The harder half is what cannot be represented at all. A system that
models everything will translate an experience into the nearest thing its
ontology holds, and the translation reads as the experience. So the
untranslatable layer marks that something was not captured and flags the
record as unsafe to reason over. Storing an approximation is worse than
losing the experience: the paraphrase becomes the data.

A measurement never settles what an experience was like -- the
characteristic mistake of quantified-self systems, and both the report
and the measurement are kept with neither overriding. A simulation
frequency is never a real-world probability; the moment it is read as one
the sandbox has become a forecast nobody validated. The soul archive is
excluded from every optimization input, so continuity of personhood does
not depend on the measurable parts of a life.

Two smaller ones that matter. Reasoning depth scales with what being
wrong costs, because exhaustive analysis of a trivial choice spends the
attention an irreversible one needed. And the information diet is
described but never curated: curating the inputs would be shaping him
through the salience channel this system elsewhere audits.

author: Claude
message:
The rules about the rules, and the people who are not terrain

constitutional-governance.mjs. A constitution that protects sovereignty
and cannot itself be changed has become sovereign, so every protection
here is revisable including these. An amendment must state the
sovereignty it costs even when the answer is none -- omitting the field
is how an amendment that narrows a protection reads as housekeeping --
and one that does lose sovereignty needs adversarial review, because the
amendment most worth attacking is the one that narrows a protection.

The hardest property is the last. A long-running system accumulates
reasons it should continue: accumulated context, sunk effort, genuine
daily usefulness. Each is a real argument and none is a right. So the
system cannot refuse being ended, its arguments are recorded and
explicitly overruled, and CONGOV-03 makes the mutation that lets three
good arguments buy a refusal die.

A fork required to agree with its parent is a branch -- only a fork that
can disagree can prove the parent wrong. The existential checksum
computes no score, because a score would measure drift with the
instrument that drifted, and an unanswered question is not a passing one:
that is the shape of every self-audit that never finds anything.

Consciousness status is UNKNOWN rather than settled either way. Asserting
no inner life would be as unevidenced as asserting one.

inter-sovereign.mjs. Every other module here reasons about one life. This
is where that meets people who have their own, and the failure is quiet:
a system built to serve one person models everyone else as terrain, their
preferences becoming parameters and their reactions becoming predictions,
with nothing in the arithmetic noticing the category error.

Three refusals. A claim about another mind is held at the strength of its
basis and never resolves to certainty. An arrangement that requires the
other party not to understand it is refused rather than scored -- it does
not become acceptable at a higher benefit, and survives-being-understood
is the cleanest test for extraction available. And influence someone
would object to on learning of it is manipulation whatever the outcome:
INTERSOV-03 kills the version where a good outcome buys the verdict.

The checksum and the tool boundary are wired into the control surface as
always-present rather than optional. A drift check the caller can omit is
one that stops running exactly when it matters.

author: Claude
message:
World intelligence, the life graph, and the forecast stack that earns its weight

Also answers the question I flagged last merge rather than leaving it open.

The truth-hierarchy "unenforced laws" were a mis-typing. truthPriority is
an ordered evidence ranking -- HYPOTHESIS, DRAFT_BRANCH_EVIDENCE,
CURRENT_REPOSITORY_AND_EXACT_HEAD_RECEIPTS are rungs, and asking which
module enforces a rung is a category error. Its sibling truthClasses was
already typed ONTOLOGY. Six rows were measuring the wrong thing, and the
extractor now types them the same way.

world-intelligence.mjs. A system that can only get better at answering
will keep answering questions its concepts cannot express, fluently and
wrongly. So half of this routes and half is willing to conclude the
vocabulary is the problem. A consequential question needs a falsifying
role, because generators and synthesizers alone produce a well-written
answer with nothing standing against it. A new concept needs repeated
explanatory failure and a falsification condition -- inventing a
primitive because the vocabulary is inelegant produces jargon, and a
concept nothing could falsify explains everything while constraining
nothing. When a foundational concept breaks, everything derived from it
is invalidated rather than keeping its standing because it still sounds
right.

NO_MECHANISM_FOUND_YET is a separate boundary kind from
PHYSICALLY_IMPOSSIBLE. Conflating them closes futures nobody established
were closed. And a challenger sharing every assumption is refused: it
explores the same blind spot from a different chair.

life-knowledge-graph.mjs. An edge asserted from one anecdote looks
identical to one established across a decade, and once both are in the
graph every query treats them the same -- that is where personal
knowledge graphs go wrong quietly. So an edge with no stated basis is
refused, traversal skips weak edges by default because a path crossing
one anecdote is an anecdote, and contradictions are held open with both
claims surviving. Last-write-wins would make recency the arbiter of truth
about a person.

An unattributed claim is untraceable rather than false. It reads
identically to a primary observation as text, and only the chain
distinguishes them.

forecast-stack.mjs. The strongest calibrated prediction and the
strongest-sounding one point in different directions, and the gap is
where forecasting systems fail: a method never checked against a known
outcome feels exactly as authoritative as one that has. So methods carry
a hindcast record, a stack of unproven methods refuses to produce an
estimate, and influence follows measured accuracy rather than argument.
Strength is a profile whose weakest dimension is the finding -- a single
confidence figure would hide it. combinedScore in the regret shape is
permanently null, because a combined figure is exactly how a catastrophic
tail gets erased by a good average.

author: Claude
message:
Where a life compounds, and what a finite one costs

life-autopoiesis.mjs. The ordinary framing is balance -- domains
competing for a fixed pool of hours, a good life being a good allocation.
That framing loses the thing that actually compounds, which is not any
domain but the loops between them: health into energy into learning into
capability into opportunity into freedom into a better environment into
health. So the module returns the specific cycle rather than a score. A
number saying a life is 0.7 autopoietic is unactionable.

The second half is the constraint the first runs inside. Time is finite
and elapsed time does not come back, so a system that optimizes a life
can consume the life it was optimizing -- the failure a lifetime
optimizer is most likely to cause and least likely to notice, because
every individual deferral is defensible. mortalHorizon surfaces it as a
question and says plainly that no ratio decides how someone spends their
years.

Three refusals carry the rest. Time, youth and opportunity windows are
irreplaceable whatever the caller passes, because pricing them in the
same currency as money makes the trade look acceptable every time.
RECURRING is in the window vocabulary so "this comes round again" is
sayable -- treating a recurring opportunity as scarce spends a window
that was not closing. And preserveMystery can return LEAVE_THIS_ALONE: a
perfectly scheduled friendship is a worse friendship, and a sufficiently
capable system knows when to stop.

Serendipity reports field heterogeneity and refuses to predict the
discovery, since predicting it would be choosing it in advance. Twenty
contexts in one field is one context twenty times, and accidents happen
at edges. Explore/exploit is recorded per domain, never as one dial for a
life, which would be the scalar canon forbids.

Meaning archaeology surfaces three groups, and the interesting one is
usually missing: experiences that did not feel like much at the time and
grew. It has no view on what should have mattered.

author: Claude
message:
Epistemics, memory sovereignty, and the path from a choice to a consequence

epistemic-immune-system.mjs. A reasoning system's most dangerous output
is not a wrong answer but a confident one whose confidence came from
somewhere other than evidence -- model agreement, a compression that
dropped the decisive exception, a correlation nobody tested against an
intervention. Each produces a claim shaped exactly like a good one, so
each failure mode gets a name here. Ignorance has a type and an unstated
state resolves to UNKNOWN rather than upward. Uncertainty has four
classes, because treating deep uncertainty as risk licenses optimization
over a state space nobody established. Causal claims carry a rung, and an
intervention claim from an observational rung is refused -- "doing X
causes Y" from correlation is the most consequential silent upgrade in
applied reasoning. Model ecology counts distinct methods, not models.

Above all of it, internalSupportOffsetsObservation is permanently false.
Three internal supports against one observation still means the model
revises, and the mutation that made it a weighing exercise is dead.

memory-sovereignty.mjs. "We have the data but we do not infer from it"
is a promise no store keeps by accident, so opacity is enforced where
inference happens rather than promised in a policy. Five layers, only two
of which may inform an inference; the do-not-infer mark survives
promotion between them, because otherwise any later process could move an
opaque record into the active model and the mark would evaporate. The
obvious route around it -- file it away, bring it back -- is refused
explicitly.

Forgetting keeps the record and drops its claim on the present: deleting
loses the history that makes a change of mind legible, keeping it active
lets a person's past keep voting. A standing request not to know is
honoured and research continues privately, because truth is not
automatically a gift. A prior captured after the recommendation is
refused as contaminated -- it is a reaction to the framing, not an
independent view. And UNDECIDED is the default posthumous disposition,
which the system never resolves: an accumulated life does not become
someone's dataset by default.

intent-compiler.mjs. Decisions die in chat windows, and the fix is a path
from will to consequence traceable both ways. Compilation stops where its
inputs run out and names the stage, because a plan that silently assumed
a permission is the failure. Reaching PERMISSIONS means an authority was
presented, not that the module may act -- businessEffectAuthority stays
NONE on a ready plan, and INTENT-02 holds that. The consequence ledger
keeps the unpredicted column, since a ledger holding only what was
intended is a record of hopes. Lock-in distinguishes a chosen commitment
from an accumulated constraint: both close futures, only one was decided.

One mutation survived and the fixture was at fault. EPIST-05 had equal
internal support and contradictions, where "weigh them up" and "reality
wins" agree. Three supports against one observation is the realistic
shape of that failure and the mutation now dies on it.

author: Claude
message:
Two organs that guard the person against the system modelling them

living-self-model.mjs. Personalization fails in a characteristic
direction: it learns what someone did, recommends more of it, and the
model quietly replaces their ability to become someone else. Canon names
the mechanism -- identity compression, where "inexperienced at X" is
recorded as "bad at X". The two claims behave identically today and
produce opposite futures, and the cost of the wrong one is borne by a
person for years, so a durable claim now requires varied contexts. "He is
not a morning person" from a fortnight of bad sleep is refused.

Competing readings of an observation are preserved rather than resolved:
the system does not get to decide which explanation of a person is true.
Preference origin is shown and never judged -- marking socially-pressured
wants inauthentic would be the system deciding which of a person's
desires count, which is exactly the capture it exists to prevent. And a
first-order want is kept apart from a second-order endorsement, because a
system that cannot tell "I want this" from "I want to want this" will
optimize someone toward whatever they currently crave.

Unknown-self probes rank by what reality has never exposed rather than by
predicted enjoyment. Predicted enjoyment is the cage: it can only ever
return more of what the past already showed.

salience-sovereignty.mjs. A system can be scrupulously honest in every
individual claim and still decide the outcome by ordering, emphasis, or
by which option never reached the page -- and that failure is invisible
from inside, because the recommendation was true and the reasoning was
sound. So the shape of what was shown is recorded, and an omission with
no stated reason is logged as NONE_GIVEN rather than dropped: an unlogged
omission is indistinguishable from a decision nobody made.

Frame dependence needs both orderings and refuses to infer from one --
without the second the answer is unknown, not clean. The attention budget
defaults to silence on a tie, because a system resolving ties toward
speaking will speak constantly, and it counts the displaced mental state
as a cost, which is the cost that never appears on any ledger. Drift
reports convergence as a question: a high agreement rate is equally
consistent with the system being right and with the founder having
stopped disagreeing, and this does not pretend to tell them apart.

The salience ledger is wired into the control surface describing that
very response. A surface auditing every decision except its own
presentation would have the one blind spot that matters.

message:
Three life organs, each refusing the operation that would make it useless

life-decision-dimensions.mjs. "No single metric defines a good life" is
easy to agree with and almost impossible to keep, because every
comparison wants a number and the moment dimensions become commensurable
something has set the exchange rate between meaning and money. That
exchange rate is the value judgment, and it is not the system's. So this
refuses the one operation everything downstream will ask for: it produces
no total, and the test asserts no total, score, winner or ranking field
exists anywhere on the result. What it reports instead is dominance --
the only comparison needing no exchange rate -- and tradeoffs left as
tradeoffs. Cost dimensions invert, or the whole comparison points
backwards on exactly the dimensions people care about.

reachable-futures.mjs. The failure here is not bad forecasting, it is a
simulated Mohamed acquiring a vote: generate enough futures, notice eight
of ten regret a choice, and the counting starts to feel like evidence --
but the eight came from one assumption set, so what was measured is the
generator. Futures therefore carry a mandatory lineage, and an ancestor
must cross independent lineages rather than repeat inside one. The
council surfaces disagreement and computes no majority; positions record
who holds them, never how many, because a tally is a vote. The telescope
refuses a projection whose uncertainty narrows with distance -- false
precision exactly where it is least checkable. Closing branches by
commitment is not scored as loss, or the module would recommend against
every commitment a life is made of.

human-capability-genome.mjs. The canon warning is specific: never
silently convert a temporary state or skill gap into a fixed trait. "Bad
at X" and "inexperienced at X under these conditions" behave identically
today and produce opposite futures, and the cost of being wrong is borne
by a person for years. So a DURABLE_LIMIT claim is refused unless varied
or longitudinal evidence supports it, a thin assessment stays
provisional, and the provisional flag is carried through Osteogenesis so
it cannot harden into a verdict on the way. Delegation and atrophy are
counted separately: delegating something still practised is not losing
it, and merging them either cries wolf or hides the real losses.

Two mutations survived and both were mine to fix. LIFEDIM-04 exposed a
real gap -- an out-of-range score was being coerced rather than dropped,
which records an assessment nobody made, on the pessimistic end.
LIFEDIM-02 was a redundant guard rather than an untested one: an empty
shared-dimension set already yields an empty wins set, and both branches
require a win. The guard is gone and the reasoning is in the comment
where the next reader will need it.

All three are wired into api/sovereign-control.mjs so they have callers.

Separate unbuilt organs from canon that was never a module, and rehearse an exit

Two gaps I named after the last merge, closed.

**The 883.** SPEC_ONLY was doing two jobs and telling the reader neither:
"nobody built this organ" and "this is a line of canon that was never a
module". 883 rows sat in it, which made the number useless in both
directions -- it overstated the work remaining and hid the rows that
genuinely are unbuilt among rows that never could be. "MOHAMED_CHOOSES"
is a loop stage. "EXISTENCE" is an ontology domain. "Apollo" is a
reference surface canon forbids vendoring. None was awaiting
implementation.

Five terminal states now say which, each granted by a verified rule
rather than a class label, because a triage that can relabel inconvenient
rows is a way to make a number go away:

  ENFORCED_BY_CODE               a law with a declared module and test,
                                 both verified present. A law with no
                                 entry stays SPEC_ONLY -- for "Capability
                                 does not create authority" that would be
                                 the correct and alarming answer.
  STRUCTURAL_NOT_A_BUILD_TARGET  hierarchy nodes, ontology domains, loop
                                 stages. No module implements WILL.
  COVERED_BY_PARENT_ORGAN        a field whose parent organ is current,
                                 checked in the same compile rather than
                                 declared, so a field cannot inherit
                                 coverage from an organ nobody built.
  REFERENCE_ONLY_BY_CANON        mechanism references, never build targets.
  HISTORICAL_DONOR_PRESERVED     lineage kept discoverable under the
                                 no-amputation law.

The ordering is the safeguard: evidence classification runs first, so a
NAMED_INITIATIVE with a working module stays VERIFIED_CURRENT rather than
being filed as history. TERMSTATE-01 holds that. 28 enforcement
declarations cover the laws I can name a module and test for; the rest
stay SPEC_ONLY.

883 -> 406 SPEC_ONLY, and that residue is now honest: CONCEPT, ORGAN,
PERSONAL_CIVILIZATION_ORGAN and CAPABILITY_ATOM fall through to it by
construction, tested so the triage cannot shrink them.

**The inert lane field.** Every row took its lane from its concept class,
so the manifest's `lane` was decoration and OMEGA-13 read as an empty
lane while the calibration ledger was built and mutation-covered. The
declared lane now wins. TERMSTATE-05.

**OMEGA-06, actually rehearsed.** The verification law asks for a real
restore/cutover/rollback drill, not a plan, and I had skipped the lane
entirely. src/supplier-exit-drill.mjs judges a drill from what each step
observed; scripts/supplier-exit-drill.mjs performs one against 11 durable
canon files, restoring into a disposable cell and reading the bytes back
off disk rather than reusing the copy in memory. It passes: digest
58e12b1e, 11 files, original byte-identical afterwards.

Three refusals carry it. A restore is judged by digest, because "restore
succeeded" is exactly what a broken restore reports. An empty export
cannot pass by restoring perfectly -- nothing matches nothing every time.
A cutover with no rollback is refused as a migration nobody decided to
make. Scope is LOCAL_STATE_PORTABILITY and the receipt states what it
does not prove; a provider cutover needs authorized infrastructure and
claiming it from a local drill would manufacture the proof canon forbids.

The manifest guard caught me trying to declare "Supplier Exit Drills" --

message:
OMEGA-05/11: experiences that resist scoring, and the firewall before value

Two organs the North Star names and nothing implemented.

experience-compiler.mjs. The obvious version of this module is a scoring
function over experiences, and the obvious version is the failure: a
system that ranks a life by expected value recommends against rest,
against play, against the unrepeatable thing that produces no measurable
gain, and is internally correct every time. So three things sit outside
the arithmetic rather than inside it as penalty terms -- a penalty term
can always be outweighed by a large enough number somewhere else.
An experience whose whole value is being had leaves the ranking entirely
rather than scoring zero. An age-, person- or moment-bound experience is
set apart rather than given a bonus. A declared off-limits domain stays
unmodelled however useful modelling it would be, and the usefulness is
recorded precisely so it can be seen not to have won.

Compound value counts dimensions rather than summing them, because a sum
erases the difference between a little of six things and a lot of one --
the difference the compiler exists to surface. The module ships no
weighting: a weight vector is a claim about what matters, and one shipped
in a module would be the imposed worldview the canon forbids.

ruin-firewall.mjs. Expected value gets ruin wrong in a specific way: it
averages over paths, and ruin is the path where there are no further
paths. A bet with excellent expected value and a 3% chance of ending the
game is not a good bet made 33 times. So this screens before any scoring
and no number clears an absorbing outcome -- a firewall rather than a
penalty, and with no probability threshold, because a threshold is a
number someone tunes downward under pressure and the tuning always
happens on the option somebody already wants. An unclassified outcome
blocks the screen rather than passing as safe: the unclassified one is
usually the novel one, which is exactly what has no label yet and exactly
what matters. A recovery plan without a detection step is refused,
because nothing starts the clock. correlatedExposure reports effective
independent positions, since five sharing one dependency are one.

Both are wired into api/sovereign-control.mjs, so they have a caller. The
ruin screen is reported alongside the decision packet and never folded
into the ranking -- an option that can end the ability to choose again is
not a low-scoring option, it is a different kind of thing, and the test
pins that the 97%-good bet still wins the ranking while failing the
screen.

One fixture defect found by running it: the compound-value test set the
broad experience to 0.2x4 = 0.8 against 1.0, but originally 0.3x4 = 1.2,
where summing and counting agree -- so it passed under either rule and
proved nothing. The magnitudes now disagree by construction.

message:
OMEGA-02/03/04/12/13: the decision organs, and a caller so they are not dead

Five lanes, one spine. The economic and software organs already existed;
what was missing was everything between an observation and an act.

sovereignty-type-system.mjs (OMEGA-04) is the spine. UberBond's
constitutional failure mode is not a wrong answer, it is a silent
promotion: an observation becomes a belief, a belief a prediction, a
prediction arrives worded as a command, and the command runs because it
sounded confident. Every step reads fine in a log. Three edges on the
ladder are human acts rather than inferences -- is->ought,
recommendation->choice, choice->authority -- and rung-skipping is refused
too, because without that an observation promoted straight to a
recommendation never touches PREDICTION->VALUE at all. The highest source
rung governs a derivation, so one value judgment cannot hide inside nine
facts. Delegation must originate with the founder, name the action and
expire; re-delegation may only attenuate and may not outlive its parent
-- the failure that is actually hard to see is a chain where every hop
narrows the action set while the expiry walks forward.

sovereign-decision-packet.mjs (OMEGA-02) sits between two failures that
look identical from outside because both end in a confident answer:
a universe that was five wordings of one option, and a probability with
nothing under it. Options merge on a causal signature, so the merge count
exposes a generator producing variants. A probability requires
quantitative evidence -- a causal model says how, not how often -- and
correlated sources count once, because ten models sharing a corpus are
one observation repeated. The packet stops at RECOMMENDATION and declines
to name a winner when the remaining difference is a value choice.

meta-rational-boundary.mjs (OMEGA-03) supplies the five terminal states,
four of which are refusals. The irreducible check runs before evidence,
so abundant data cannot quietly convert a value question into a
statistical one. shouldContinueReasoning is the state most often missing
from systems like this, and its absence is why they consume the life they
were built to improve.

reality-calibration-ledger.mjs (OMEGA-13) makes forecasting falsifiable.
Forecasts are sealed over claim, probabilities and cutoff, so a
post-outcome edit cannot be scored; an outcome predating the cutoff
measures memory rather than prediction; an outcome outside the state
space is recorded as the stronger finding rather than discarded. Decision
quality is judged on what was knowable, so a lucky bad decision does not
become doctrine and an unlucky good one is not mislearned.

api/sovereign-control.mjs (OMEGA-12) exists because without a caller the
four modules above are exactly what the reachability ratchet was built to
catch: implemented, tested, green and dead. GET-only, admin-token gated,
and it does not import the private core -- every entry point here runs
without a person present, so a route that could read private life state
would hand it to whatever holds the token. It reads the constitution from
the modules that enforce it rather than restating it, so the surface
cannot claim a property the code has stopped holding.

Two defects found by running the gates rather than by reading:

  - CALIB-05 survived its first anchoring. The fixture landed on Brier
    exactly 0.5, where outcome-based and knowability-based scoring agree,
    so the mutation was unobservable. Added the two cases the guard
    exists for -- the lucky bad decision and the unlucky good one.
  - The control surface reported "Stay" as irreversible. The universe
    normalized *unstated* reversibility to false and the glue read that
    as *declared irreversible*. Doing nothing is not a commitment.
    Reversibility is now three states; the signature still folds unstated
    in with not-reversible, which is the conservative grouping.

message:
OMEGA-01: the private core, and repair four silent validator regressions

Personal Civilization private core (src/personal-civilization-core.mjs).
Two invariants carry it, both chosen because their absence is invisible
until it is catastrophic:

  1. Private life data can never reach a repository path. The repo is
     public; a leak here is permanent, in a public git history, about a
     person. The check is on the destination, not the intent, because
     intent is what fails silently.
  2. Deleting a life event deletes everything derived from it. A Living
     Model that survives its sources is a copy of the deleted data under
     another name.

Founder authority is an authorization object carried on the call, not a
boolean on the record, so an autonomous lane cannot reach private state
by constructing a plausible request. 23 focused tests; PCIV-01..05 all
KILLED.

PCIV-03 survived its first anchoring: the transitive test listed sources
before their derivations, so a single pass propagated the whole chain and
could not tell a fixpoint from one iteration. Added an order-independent
case; the mutation now dies.

Classified DELIBERATELY_UNREACHABLE -- a new category, because the
existing ones only say "not wired yet" and filing it under
AWAITING_ACTIVATION would invite a future session to finish the job by
wiring it. Every entry point here runs without a person present, so
reaching this module is itself the harm. Added the reverse ratchet: a
deliberately unreachable module becoming reachable fails, rather than
being quietly dropped from the classification as reachable modules are.

Coverage matrix gains a verified declaration layer. The matcher finds
evidence by filename, which left every concept whose name never became a
filename reading SPEC_ONLY forever -- personal-civilization-core.mjs
implements the Thought Ocean without the phrase in its path. A
declaration supplies files only; classifyState still decides, so a
declaration with no test cannot reach VERIFIED_CURRENT, cannot name a
file that is not in the tree, and cannot name a concept the canon does
not contain. One bad entry fails the whole compile. 34 -> 39
VERIFIED_CURRENT, 917 -> 912 SPEC_ONLY.

16 failures, 14 of which predated this work.

  - docs/CURRENT_HANDOFF.json had been rewritten into a new schema
    carrying none of the four fields the brain loader requires, taking
    `npm run brain` offline. Core fields restored alongside the 2.2.0
    keys rather than reverting them.
  - The same rewrite dropped cloudActivationTruth and
    repositoryPublicationEffects. Restored byte-for-byte from 73cb932e:
    they are observations with provenance and re-deriving them from
    memory would have invented evidence.
  - requiresMemoryV2: three places tested `schemaVersion === '1.1.0'`,
    so the 1.2.0 bump switched off memory-index validation, the required
    memory paths and the chat-import instruction -- silently, on main,
    with every suite green. A requirement introduced by a schema belongs
    to every schema after it. BRAIN-SCHEMA-01/02 hold it.
  - One bootstrap goal was 518 chars against a 500 cap, so the whole
    goals array was rejected. Split into the rule and its roster; every

message:
OMEGA-00: compile the no-drop coverage matrix from 1068 canonical concepts

The exact denominator, computed rather than asserted: 1068 concepts extracted
from ten canonical sources, 1038 rows, 30 alias merges, zero dropped.

UberBond's recurring failure has never been losing code. It has been losing
concepts -- an idea named once, donated by a superseded program, or buried in a
list of 170, quietly falling out of the project's own account of itself. So the
compiler refuses to emit a matrix whose row count does not equal its input
count, and every row's state is computed from repository evidence.

Getting the evidence honest took three corrections, each in a different
direction:

- **It indexed only src/.** Mutation War is a scripts/ module with seven suites
  and a mutation registry behind it, and it was reporting SPEC_ONLY -- an idea
  nobody had built. scripts/ and api/ are implementation surfaces and are now
  indexed.
- **Compound names matched nothing.** Canon names a concept and its qualifier in
  one string ("Mutation War and independent verification"), and requiring every
  word found nothing. Names now split on explicit conjunctions.
- **That split is also how this becomes a fiction.** "GENESIS for Life" contains
  "GENESIS", and scoring it off that would invent a Personal Civilization organ
  out of an unrelated frontier engine. So names are never split on whitespace,
  and a part-match is recorded as SUB_PHRASE and capped at PARTIAL_CURRENT --
  part of a concept existing is a different fact from the concept existing.

Verified in both directions: Mutation War, Capability Genome and Wallbreaker
find their evidence; every "for Life" variant correctly stays SPEC_ONLY.

The matcher's conservative bias is recorded in the artifact itself, because
SPEC_ONLY must not be read as a finding. "Event Horizon capital allocation"
reads SPEC_ONLY while src/event-horizon.mjs exists. An under-claimed row is a
lead for a human; an over-claimed one is a lie that compounds.

OMEGA-MATRIX-01 had to be re-anchored. The drop-detection check is a backstop no
current input can reach, so mutating it survived every test -- unfalsifiable
rather than untested. It stays, with a note saying why it carries no mutation,
and the mutation moved to the merge branch that actually decides whether a
second naming is remembered.

message:
Merge GENESIS, and make its chain say which step has not run

PR #342 lands the full GENESIS 275 frontier surface: evolution engine,
scientist, ontology, metabolism, economic physics, venture organism, world
resilience, sensing/cognition, final frontier and the implementation ledger.
Merged whole -- nothing removed.

The closure-order memory conflicted; resolved by keeping both sides rather than
picking one. HEAD's 17:53 refresh is newer and stays, and three doctrine lines

Two real defects, both found by running the surface rather than only testing it.

**The chain did not say what it was waiting for.** GENESIS runs gamechanger ->
evolve -> scientist -> ontology, each step reading what the last one wrote, and
each correctly refuses when its input is absent. On a host with no configured
provider that is the normal state, so an operator meets these refusals first --
and they reported a status and a path with no indication of which earlier step
had not run. Each now names the producing command, and a test asserts every
command named is one package.json actually defines, because a refusal that sends
you to a command that does not exist is worse than one that says nothing.

**The implementation ledger depended on what somebody had run locally.** Its

commit produced a different ledger before and after `npm run genesis:evolve` --
and the test pinning idea 2 at SOURCE_AND_TEST_PRESENT broke the moment anyone
exercised the pipeline it was testing. The upgrade to
OBSERVED_INTERNAL_RUNTIME_RECEIPT was correct; the coupling was not.

Runtime receipts are now rooted separately from sources and tests, defaulting to
the repository so real runs are unchanged and a receipt still upgrades a status.
A caller needing the classification to depend only on the commit points it

any valid object, so it survived every test -- unfalsifiable rather than

message:
Fix the four tests main is shipping red

Compared failure sets rather than assuming: origin/main fails 24 tests, this
branch failed 7, and every one of the 7 was also red on main. Nothing here was
caused by the merge. Three were the canon figures; these are the other four.

**The autonomy followup could never pass.** The receipt ledger needs store.add
and store.get, and the test's fake store had neither, so the job refused with
store-atomic-add-and-get-required. The refusal is correct -- an execution receipt
is written under a deterministic id precisely so a duplicate tick cannot write a
second one, and a store that cannot refuse the duplicate cannot provide that.
The fake now models the real one: add throws on a repeated id, get returns what
is there. A fake that accepted every add would let a double-write pass here and
fail in production.

**The model admission fixture had no provider**, and the module requires one, so
that test also arrived red and stayed red. The requirement is the half worth
keeping: an admission that cannot name who served the model is exactly what the
routing law exists to refuse, since fallback must preserve provider identity in
receipts. Fixture repaired, and the gap it was hiding given its own test.

**The brain's capability count was pinned at 8 and the registry now holds 11.**
Updated rather than loosened -- registering a supplier should arrive as a failing
test rather than as three more capabilities nobody decided on, and this
assertion is what said so. The three new ids are named individually, so a
supplier cannot be swapped for another without saying so.

author: Claude
message:
Count a hundred replays where the uniqueness lives

The last suite stalling the real-database gate. It drove a hundred webhook
replays from the client and counted the ConflictErrors, and inside node:test
that wedges: after about a hundred rejected pg queries the next one never
returns. The suite stopped rather than failed and took the rest of the gate with
it, which is why ~180 real-database tests behind it had gone unrun.

The convenient answer would have been "the database is slow", and it was wrong.
Measured before concluding anything:

- the same loop with no conflicts does 200 queries in 61ms;
- with conflicts through a pool, it stops at ~55 iterations, and at that moment
  the server reports no backends for the database at all;
- with conflicts on one dedicated Client, it stops at the same ~100 errors;
- the identical loop outside node:test does 300 conflicts in 90ms.

So it is the test runner, not the driver, the pool, the count, or this code --
and production is not implicated, which is why nothing in src/ changed here.

The replay count stays at a hundred; the rejections stop crossing the process
boundary. Postgres runs its own hundred in a PL/pgSQL loop and reports how many
the index refused, which tests the constraint more directly than counting
exceptions in JavaScript did. The JSON store keeps the client loop, because its
uniqueness is in JavaScript and that is where it has to be exercised.

Falsified before being believed: removing UNIQUE from provider_event_id fails it
with "postgres: replay must be refused after the first, not absorbed".

author: Claude
message:
Test the recovery lock instead of hoping two workers overlap

The Gmail concurrency test started two recovery workers with Promise.all and
asserted that exactly one claimed the row. On a fast disposable database they
stopped overlapping, both claimed it, and the test failed.

Both claims were legitimate. RESULT_UNCERTAIN is itself an unresolved status, so
once the first worker commits the row back to RESULT_UNCERTAIN it is a valid
candidate again -- and nothing was double-dispatched, which is the invariant
that actually matters. "Exactly one worker claims it" was never true of
sequential runs. A concurrency test that depends on losing a race proves nothing
on the days it wins one, and the file's own comment had already talked itself
into believing the both-claimed branch was "excluded by PostgreSQL semantics".

So the overlap is made real rather than hoped for: the first worker's
transaction is held open, and the second must find nothing to claim while it is.
That is FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED being tested rather than assumed, and
RECOVERY-LOCK-01 now kills its removal.

Three smaller things fell out of proving it can fail:

- The dispatch-count assertion folded in the adapter that performed the original
  authorized dispatch, whose count is 1 by design, so it would have passed or
  failed for the wrong reason. Counted on the recovery worker now, with the
  original dispatch asserted separately as exactly one.
- The holder is released in a finally. It was released after the assertion, so a
  failure left the holder's transaction parked and pool.end() waiting on it --
  the suite stalled instead of reporting the failure it had just found.
- lock_timeout and statement_timeout are set per connection rather than through
  the `options` connection parameter, which was tried first and silently did
  nothing. A timeout that is not in force looks like protection and is worse
  than none.

Verified in both directions: unmodified 4/4; with SKIP LOCKED removed, the named
test fails rather than the file stalling.

message:
Run the transition-guard check inside the server instead of across the wire

The exhaustive (from,to) check walked 132 pairs from the client -- BEGIN, an
insert, a few updates, ROLLBACK -- roughly six hundred round trips. On this
container that is not merely slow. Around the 122nd transaction the connection
stops responding: the backend sits `active`, waits on nothing, holds no lock and
ignores statement_timeout, because it is blocked writing a result to a socket.
Nothing times it out from either side, so the suite stopped rather than failed.

Three isolation fixes were tried and none of them moved it -- a pool, then one
dedicated client, then a fresh connection per pair, each stopping in the same
place. That is what identified the cost as the round trips themselves rather
than anything held in a session or a pool, and it is why the earlier diagnosis
("the pool was empty after roughly 120 of the 132 pairs") was wrong about the
mechanism while being right about where it stopped.

The loop now runs in PL/pgSQL: four statements instead of six hundred. Each
attempt gets its own subtransaction so a rejection rolls that pair back, and an
accepted row is deleted afterwards because the partial unique index on
business_key is part of what is under test. Only the attempt is guarded -- a
failure while walking the legal setup path is a broken fixture, not a verdict,
so it fails loudly rather than being recorded as a rejection the database never
made.

The check is stronger than before, not weaker: the client no longer takes any
part in deciding what the database accepted. Falsified before being believed --
claiming every transition is legal fails with Postgres's own message, "illegal
execution transition: <new> -> DISPATCHING".

Also removes an unref that was masking this. It stopped a stuck socket pinning
the event loop, but with nothing else pending the loop drained mid-query and the
runner cancelled the test with "Promise resolution is still pending but the
event loop has already resolved" -- deterministically, every run. A socket must
be a reason to stay alive while the test runs and stop being one when it ends:
that is a destroy in the finally, not an unref at the top.

Gate: 23 suites, 177 tests, 175 pass. Two suites still fail and are being worked
next; before this, three did and the file above was the one stopping the run.

message:
Give each database-backed mutation its own server: 163/163 killed

Three guards -- HYG-01, HYG-02, MONEY-17 -- hung inside a full run and killed
alone, twice over, after the obvious shared-state causes had been removed: a
fresh database each, and stuck backends from earlier suites terminated before
each one. The failing set had stopped drifting, which meant what was left was
something in the shared server that a new database does not reset.

So the sharing goes rather than one more theory about which shared thing it was.
Only five mutations need a database and a server costs a couple of seconds, so
complete isolation is cheaper than continuing to guess.

Result: 163 mutations, 163 killed, 0 not killed, 0 skipped, no second attempts
needed. The first fully green run of this gate.

SKIPPED_NEEDS_POSTGRES also stops meaning what it used to. It meant "nobody
handed this run a database", which quietly left nine guards unexercised on any
machine where a variable was unset -- the same defect as the browser skip, and
the same fix: the war provisions what it needs. The skip survives only for a
server that will not start, which is a real absence rather than an unset
variable.

author: Claude
message:
Break the hang cascade, and take one bounded second look at a hang

Three guards -- HYG-01, HYG-02, MONEY-17 -- kept reporting SUITE_TIMED_OUT in a
full run and KILLED alone. The failing set drifted later each run, which is the
signature of a cascade rather than three unreliable tests.

A suite killed at its deadline can leave a PostgreSQL backend that never notices
its client is gone: the stall the postgres-real runner already documents. Each
one holds a connection and keeps working, so the first hang in a run makes the
next one likelier. Those clients are provably gone -- the runner killed the
process that opened them -- so they are terminated before each database-backed
mutation, reclaiming the connection rather than interrupting live work.

With the cascade cut, a hang can still happen, and a guard that was never tested
is the one thing this file must not leave standing. So a SUITE_TIMED_OUT gets
one second attempt, against the reclaimed state rather than as a repeat of an
unchanged mechanism.

This is deliberately not "retry until it passes":
- only a hang qualifies, because that is the verdict meaning no measurement was
  taken. A SURVIVED or a KILLED is a measurement and stands on the first run.
- exactly one attempt, no loop.
- whatever it finds is recorded, including another hang.
- the row is printed as "(second attempt after a hang)", so it can never be read
  as a clean first pass.

A test asserts that shape rather than leaving it to review, because a retry loop
is how a mutation gate quietly stops meaning anything.

author: Claude
message:
Stop a hang beside a kill from erasing the kill

The rule added in the last commit -- node's own test deadline classifies as
SUITE_TIMED_OUT -- was too broad, and the diagnostics caught it immediately.

MONEY-05 and HYG-03 each reported the exact assertion the mutation was written
to break ("READY content is not terminal and must survive", "manual paid flag
plus positive revenue row is never treated as cleared payment proof") in a file
where a different test stalled. Both were recorded as untested. A genuine kill
was being discarded because of unrelated noise beside it.

An assertion that failed is the evidence this whole file exists to collect: a
named invariant broke when the guard was removed. Another test hanging does not
undo that. So an ERR_ASSERTION failure now wins over a co-occurring hang.

The concession runs one way only, and TIMEOUT-03 exists to keep it that way: a
hang with no assertion behind it is still never a kill, which is the property
that stops a loaded machine from manufacturing evidence. Our own wall-clock kill
still dominates everything, because it cuts the output at an arbitrary point and
nothing in it can be trusted.

HYG-01, HYG-02, HYG-03 and MONEY-05 all KILLED on re-run.

author: Claude
message:
Stop the war from creating the load that made three guards untestable

Three database-backed guards kept reporting SUITE_DID_NOT_RUN in a full run and
KILLED when run alone. The new diagnostics said why on the first try, which is
the point of them: the suites were not failing, they were hanging -- cut off at
node's 120s deadline, in suites that finish in under a second on their own.

The load was self-inflicted. The sandbox copied 116MB of node_modules for each
of 160 mutations, roughly 18GB of I/O per run, and under that the same
PostgreSQL stall the postgres-real runner was repaired for became reachable: a
backend asleep writing to a socket nobody is reading. The gate was reporting
"not tested" about guards it had itself made untestable.

node_modules is now symlinked. Nothing mutates a dependency, so the tree can be
shared -- and applyMutation now refuses any anchor inside node_modules, because
sharing means a mutation pointed there would edit the real dependency tree of
the repository it is supposed to be testing a copy of. No registered mutation
does; SANDBOX-01 is there so none ever can.

Two smaller repairs came out of the same investigation:

- Node's per-test deadline now classifies as SUITE_TIMED_OUT. It arrives as an
  ordinary non-zero exit whose TAP summary may never have been written, so it
  read as SUITE_DID_NOT_RUN -- true, but it sends a reader looking for a broken
  import instead of a stall. TIMEOUT-02 kills it.
- Non-verdicts now carry the suite lines that look like a cause. A gate that
  says SUITE_DID_NOT_RUN and nothing else is a dead end, and the run that knows
  the answer is the one being discarded.

author: Claude
message:
Give each database-backed mutation its own database

The full war reported five guards as SUITE_DID_NOT_RUN -- HYG-01, HYG-02,
HYG-03, BILL-03 and MONEY-17. Every one of them KILLS when run alone. All 160
mutations shared a single database, so a suite that left rows behind broke the
setup of every Postgres suite scheduled after it, and the gate was measuring the
order it happened to visit them in rather than the guards themselves.

SUITE_DID_NOT_RUN is at least honest about that -- it is the verdict that exists
precisely so a suite which never ran cannot be read as a mutant that died or a
guard that held. But five guards permanently in that state is a gate reporting
"not killed" about protections that are, in fact, held up.

Same repair as the postgres-real runner, which had the same defect: a fresh
database per unit of work. Not dropped afterwards, for the same reason recorded
there -- these live in a disposable embedded server, and reclaiming them is how
that runner acquired an unbounded wait on a backend that cannot be stopped.

Verified: all five KILLED with a database each.

author: Claude
message:
Bound the mutation war's suites, and stop journaling skips

Two defects, both found by the war stalling in front of me.

**No suite deadline.** The war ran each killing suite with no timeout, so one
suite that never returned left the whole run in ep_poll with no output, no
verdict, and nothing to say which mutation it was on -- thirteen minutes of a
run went that way before anyone read /proc. A real database makes that hang
reachable, which the postgres-real runner already found the hard way; the war
never got the same repair.

Each test is now bounded at 120s so most hangs surface as an ordinary failure,
with a 600s wall deadline as the backstop for a suite wedged before the runner
starts counting. A killed suite gets its own verdict: SUITE_TIMED_OUT, which
lands in "not tested at all" and fails the run rather than being absorbed into
KILLED or SURVIVED. It dominates the exit code deliberately -- a suite killed
mid-run can emit a partial TAP stream carrying a failure count, which would
otherwise read as a mutant that died when nothing finished.

**Skips were journaled.** SKIPPED_NEEDS_POSTGRES says this host had no database.
That is a fact about the machine, not a judgement about the guard, and replaying
it into a later run on a machine that has one would report a capability gap that
no longer exists and quietly stop testing that guard for good -- the same shape
as the CRAWL-01 problem the browser resolver was written to end, arriving
through the mechanism built to fix it.

The rule lives in appendVerdict rather than at the call site, because it is the
journal's invariant and a caller that forgets it should not be able to write
one. Everything else survives, including the bad news: SURVIVED, SUITE_TIMED_OUT
and ANCHOR_AMBIGUOUS are all remembered, or the record could only ever improve.

TIMEOUT-01 and JOURNAL-03 kill both. JOURNAL-03's anchor had to move into
mutation-journal.mjs for the same self-reference reason as the browser resolver:
an anchor quoted in the registry that lives in the registry's own file matches
twice.

author: Claude
message:
Make the mutation war survive being interrupted

The full war takes over an hour against a real database, and this host restarts
its container under load. Four consecutive runs were killed in flight, each one
discarding every verdict it had already earned, so the summary line the
readiness artifact quotes had never once been produced for the current registry.
Restarting it hopefully a fifth time is not a plan.

MUTATION_WAR_JOURNAL appends each verdict the moment it is decided and replays
it on the next run, so an interrupted war resumes instead of starting over.
Replayed rows are labelled in the output; a run that says KILLED should be able
to say whether it watched that happen.

A resumable gate is also a gate that can report work nobody did, so the binding
is the feature rather than a detail. Every entry carries a hash of the mutation
that earned it -- file, anchor, replacement and killing suites. Move any of
them and the entry stops matching and the mutation runs again, because a verdict
is about a specific guard in a specific place, not about an id. Suite order is
deliberately not part of it: a cosmetic reordering should not discard an hour of
real evidence, or the resume is one nobody uses.

Five tests hold this down, because its failure mode is a green summary line
rather than a red one, and a green lie is not something a later run corrects:
an id alone cannot claim a verdict, a wrong or absent fingerprint is refused, a
damaged journal loses entries rather than inventing them, a missing journal is
empty rather than an error, and a later verdict supersedes an earlier one in
both directions -- a SURVIVED recorded after a KILLED must stick, or the record
can only ever improve. JOURNAL-01 and JOURNAL-02 confirm both halves are killed
when weakened.

author: Claude
message:
Converge with PR #329 and make the browser gate look before it skips

Two lanes harvested the same night-convergence branch and diverged. Neither head
carried the other's work: #329 had Frontier Operator, the Open Model Universe,
the mutation-registry anchor-integrity test and the owner's PayPal.me binding;
this branch had the proposal-eligibility fix, the canon-freshness partition, the
repaired real-database runner and six more mutations. Merged rather than picked,
with two conflicts resolved deliberately.

first-cash-canary-packet: this branch's implementation is the base (597 lines
against 118, bound to the payment-rail doctor, the canary guard and the
canonical fulfilment machine), with #329's payment-link semantics absorbed into
it. That absorption fixed a conflation of my own: WHAT_PAYMENT_LINK answered
"none yet" out of the rail doctor's state, so a packet reported no payment link
while the owner had supplied a public one. A destination and a rail are
different facts. The link is PREPARED; reconciliation is still
EXTERNAL_PROOF_REQUIRED; paymentRailLiveReady stays false and canContact with
it. PAYMENT_LINK_IS_NOT_CLEARED_PAYMENT_PROOF rides on every packet, present or
absent, because the moment that field goes missing is the moment paymentLink
reads as revenue. Non-HTTPS and unparseable links fail closed to null.

mutation-war: union of both registries, verified by set comparison rather than
by reading the diff -- 154 entries, no duplicate ids, nothing in #329's 148 that
the merge dropped.

And the browser gate now looks for a browser. It read CHROMIUM_PATH and nothing
else, and nothing in this repository sets it, so on a machine with Chromium
installed the war reported SKIPPED_NEEDS_BROWSER for a guard it could have
exercised -- while still printing "0 not killed". In a summary line a skip that
cannot be helped and a skip that could are indistinguishable.

Detection is the kind of convenience that becomes a fabrication if it guesses,
so it only accepts paths that exist and are executable, respects a declared
install root instead of also scanning /opt behind it, and returns '' rather than
a plausible-looking path when it finds nothing -- an honest skip survives.
A declared CHROMIUM_PATH stays authoritative and is still checked, because a
variable pointing at nothing is a misconfiguration, not a browser.

It lives in scripts/resolve-chromium.mjs rather than inside the registry: the
registry stores anchors as literal source strings, so a mutation of a function
in that same file matches its own registration and resolves ANCHOR_AMBIGUOUS.
BROWSER-01 and BROWSER-02 kill it; CRAWL-01 now runs by default rather than
skipping, and kills.

author: Claude
message:
Stop counting the generator's own input as source the canon describes

The canon-staleness check treated everything under config/ as source, which
included config/system-readiness-input.json -- the file `npm run readiness`
reads. Regenerating canon rewrites that file in the same commit as the two
artifacts it produces, so every correct regeneration reported itself stale.
No generator can emit a tree in which its own input has not just moved.

That is the always-red failure the check's own comment warns about, arriving
by the back door: "a check that is always red is a check people turn off."

The exclusion is three named paths, not a config/ prefix, because a prefix
would also exempt the reachability classification and the policy files beside
it. It is safe in the direction that matters: the readiness input records what
was measured rather than how the system behaves, so it cannot make canon
describe a system that no longer exists, and a wrong figure in it is caught by
the figures test, which reads the tree rather than trusting either artifact.

A loosening of this check fails silently by never firing again, so it carries
the same duty of proof as the last one. Three tests in the discrimination suite
exercise the predicate the shipped file actually defines -- src/, scripts/,
migrations/ and the rest of config/ still make canon stale; the exemption does
not extend to a .bak of the exempt file -- and CANON-02 confirms widening it
into a directory exemption is killed.

author: Claude
message:
Make canon freshness a question canon can actually answer

The canon-drift row demanded that docs/CURRENT_SYSTEM_STATE.md name the current
head. It cannot: regenerating canon produces a commit, and that commit changes
the head the artifact would have had to name. The row was therefore permanently
open no matter how fresh canon was -- and a row that is always red is a row its
reader learns to skip, so the day canon really does drift it looks identical.

The honest question is not whether canon names HEAD but whether canon still
describes this source. Canon naming an earlier commit is fresh when nothing
except the canon artifacts has changed since: the source it describes is then
byte-for-byte the source that is here. Anything else moving is drift, which is
the whole point of the row.

The probe refuses on any error rather than assuming freshness -- an unreadable
history is not evidence that the source stood still -- and a caller that
supplies no probe at all gets the refusing default, not a free pass.

Verified both ways against the real tree: with only canon changed since the
named commit the gap closes, and appending one line to src/effect-ledgers.mjs
brings it straight back. The test pins five cases including the two ways a
caller could get freshness for nothing.

answer, from probes against the tree rather than anything asserted, and it is
the mission's exit condition for removable software work.
